skill.name: helpdesk-automation
skill.description: Automate read-only HelpDesk ticket workflows through Rube MCP, including ticket lists, views, canned responses, and custom fields.
skill.summary: Automate read-only HelpDesk ticket browsing and support metadata review through Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around tool names, parameters, and fenced examples. The hardcoded Rube MCP URL is a real low severity network dependency, and the skill routes support data through a third-party MCP integration. No prompt injection or malicious command execution evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Markdown formatting triggers external command alerts.
remediation.suggestion: Add a manifest note that the skill contains documentation only and does not execute local shell or Ruby commands.

remediation.issue: Rube MCP receives access to HelpDesk data.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to approve Composio Rube access only for trusted accounts and permitted support data.

remediation.issue: Authentication happens through an external MCP setup flow.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to verify the rube.app domain and requested HelpDesk authorization scope before completing authentication.

static_findings.snippet: - Active HelpDesk connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `helpdesk`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k

1. `HELPDESK_LIST_TICKETS` - List tickets with sorting and pagination [Required]
- Forward pagination requires both `next.value` and `next.ID` from previous response
- `silo` determines which folder to list from; default is active tickets
- Response data may be nested under `data` or `data.data`
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Keep page sizes reasonable to avoid timeouts

content.value_statement: Support teams need fast access to ticket queues and reusable response assets. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through read-only HelpDesk workflows.
actual_capabilities: Connects to HelpDesk through Rube MCP after an active connection is confirmed.
Lists HelpDesk tickets by folder, sort field, sort order, page size, and cursor values.
Lists saved HelpDesk views for agent ticket organization.
Retrieves canned response templates for common support replies.
Lists custom field definitions and related validation context.
Prompts schema discovery with RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS before workflows run.
limitations: Requires an active Rube MCP server and HelpDesk connection.
Current workflows are read-only for listing and inspection tasks.
Does not create, update, move, or reply to tickets.
Pagination requires cursor values from prior responses.

use_cases.title: Review Ticket Queues
use_cases.description: Review active, archived, trashed, or spam ticket queues by folder, date ordering, and page size before daily triage.

use_cases.title: Prepare Reply Context
use_cases.description: Find canned responses and custom fields before drafting consistent replies in the HelpDesk interface.

use_cases.title: Build Read-Only Workflows
use_cases.description: Validate Rube MCP schemas and design ticket browsing workflows around cursor pagination.

prompt_templates.title: List Active Tickets
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the helpdesk automation skill to list active HelpDesk tickets. Search the current Rube tool schema first. Sort by last message date in descending order.

prompt_templates.title: Browse Archived Tickets
prompt_templates.prompt: List archived HelpDesk tickets with a page size of 25. Include the next cursor values in plain text for follow-up browsing.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Response Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: List canned responses and custom fields. Summarize which templates may fit a billing question, but do not send any reply.

prompt_templates.title: Build Paginated Triage Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Rube tool schemas, list tickets across tickets and archive folders with cursor pagination, and produce a concise triage summary with next cursor values.

output_examples.input: List active tickets sorted by most recent update.
output_examples.output: A concise ticket page summary with ticket count, sort order, key ticket identifiers, and next cursor values for continued browsing.

output_examples.input: Show available canned responses and custom fields for onboarding tickets.
output_examples.output: A grouped catalog of reusable response templates and custom field definitions that may support onboarding cases.

output_examples.input: Browse the next page using cursor values from the previous response.
output_examples.output: A follow-up page summary with first and last ticket dates, pagination direction, and remaining cursor guidance in plain text.

best_practices: Search the current Rube tool schema before each workflow.
Confirm HelpDesk connection status before requesting ticket data.
Keep page sizes conservative and record cursor values.
anti_patterns: Do not assume tool schemas or parameters are unchanged.
Do not request ticket changes or replies through read-only workflows.
Do not send sensitive ticket exports to unapproved systems.

faq.question: Does this skill create or update tickets?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflows focus on listing tickets, views, canned responses, and custom fields.

faq.question: What connection is required?
faq.answer: You need Rube MCP available and an active HelpDesk connection through the helpdesk toolkit.

faq.question: Why does it search tool schemas first?
faq.answer: Rube tool schemas can change. Searching first helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use current parameters.

faq.question: Can it browse archived or trashed tickets?
faq.answer: Yes. It can list tickets from supported folders such as active, archive, trash, and spam.

faq.question: Does it handle pagination?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains cursor-based pagination with timestamp and ID cursor values.

faq.question: What data should users protect?
faq.answer: Users should protect ticket content, customer identifiers, canned responses, custom fields, and account authorization scopes.
